title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a 'Récapitulation partielle'. It packages a free Z/4-module M of rank 2 (the shape of level-4 structures, E[4] ≅ (Z/4)^2) into finite combinatorial torsor data.

(a) Octahedron. Let M* be the 12 primitive vectors of M. Then Δ_M = M*/±1 is the 6-point set P^1(Z/4) = X_M(Z/4). Reduction mod 2 maps it 2:1 onto P^1(F_2) = (M/2M)* = M_0* = J, a 3-element set. The fibres are the antipodal pairs, so Δ is the vertex set of an unoriented octahedron whose three diagonals form J. This is the classical octahedral configuration of the 6 cusps of X(4).

(b) Faces. Faces of Δ are choices of one vertex in each diagonal, so there are 8 of them. I_M = faces/antipodism is a 4-element set. Faces are checkerboard-2-colourable, and antipodal faces have opposite colours, so F(Δ) ≅ I × C_Δ, where C_Δ is the 2-element set of 'couleurs'. Grothendieck notes three further facts:
- I is a torsor under V_4 ≅ M_0.
- J ≅ P_{2,2}(I), the 3 partitions of I into two pairs (the S_4 → S_3 map).
- I_M ≅ P_M/F_2^ω.

(c) The square. P_M is the set of set-theoretic sections ξ: M_0* → M of reduction satisfying ξ_λ + ξ_μ + ξ_ν = 0 over the three nonzero vectors. It has 16 elements and is a torsor under Hom(M_0, 2M) ≅ End(M_0) ≅ M_2(F_2). Grothendieck splits End(M_0) ≅ M_0 ⊕ F_2^ω, and this splitting is canonical:
- The two elements of order 3 of GL(M_0) ≅ S_3 are the two cyclic orders of J, i.e. ω = ω_J. Together with 0 and 1 they form the canonical subfield F_4 ≅ F_2^ω.
- The F_4-antilinear part is {0} ∪ {the three transvections}, which is ≅ M_0 by sending each transvection to its fixed vector.

Hence Q_M = P_M/M_0 is an F_2^ω-torsor. It is a 'combinatorial square' (4-cycle, automorphism group D_4) whose codiagonals (pairs of opposite edges) are ω. Similarly I_M = P_M/F_2^ω.

The data (a) and (b) depend only on the projective line X_M = P(M) over Z/4, but Q_M does not. Formula (50) lists three canonical bijections of 2-element sets (Z/2-torsors):
- codiagonals of Q ≅ ω_Δ ≅ ω_I ≅ ω_J =: ω;
- diagonals of Q ≅ face colours of Δ ≅ ω ∧ μ;
- orientations of Q ≅ or(Δ) ≅ det(M)* =: μ.

These match the abelianisation characters of the groups involved:
- O_h ≅ S_4 × Z/2 ≅ PGL_2(Z/4) has abelianisation (Z/2)^2 with characters sign(S_4) = ω, orientation = det = μ, and their product = face colour. The central inversion reverses orientation, swaps colours and fixes I.
- D_4 has abelianisation (Z/2)^2 with characters action on diagonals, action on codiagonals, and orientation, where diagonals = codiagonals ∧ orientation.

The previous page uses this to write GL(M) as a fibre product S_I ×_{±1} D_Q and M as a triple (I, Q, K: C_Q ≅ ω_I). The next page relativises to finite étale degree-4 covers I over a base S and the level-2 curve Σ_J. So the page serves Grothendieck's description of level-4 structure on elliptic curves (X(4) over X(2)) by octahedral/torsor data in a stack-theoretic, base-free form.
errors: No mathematical error found. Grothendieck writes the splitting End(M_0) ≅ M_0 ⊕ F_2^ω without justification; it is canonical, via the F_4 subring {0, 1, g, g²} and the antilinear part {0} ∪ transvections.
The defining condition of P_M is likely ξ_λ + ξ_μ + ξ_ν = 0 over the three nonzero λ, μ, ν; '(ξ_λ + ξ_μ = 0)' as transcribed would be wrong.
'F/Δ ≃ I × C_Δ' should read F(Δ) ≃ I × C_Δ, i.e. faces of Δ, not a quotient by Δ.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, canonical (choice-free, stack-friendly) torsor repackaging of a rank-2 Z/4-module via octahedron and square. It is correct and elegant, but each ingredient is classical: the octahedral X(4) and the abelianisation characters. It is a working summary rather than a new result.
transcription_corrections: The condition is probably 'ξ_λ + ξ_μ + ξ_ν = 0', not 'ξ_λ + ξ_μ = 0'.
'P_{22}(I_M)' means the set of partitions of I_M into two 2-element subsets.
'F/Δ ≃ I × C_Δ' is better read 'F(Δ) ≃ I × C_Δ'.
'ω_Q' in the last line of (50) is or(Q), the orientations of Q.
